title: Stop VNI West — Sign the Petition
lede: 85-metre steel towers across productive Victorian farmland — without genuine community consent, and without the underground option ever being properly costed. Sign the petition demanding the project be halted, now.
photoCaption: PHOTO HERE — VNI West corridor · Western Victoria

argument.h2: This isn't a transmission line. It's an imposition on the West.
argument.lede: The Victoria–NSW Interconnect West (VNI West) is being pushed through with the kind of speed Governments reserve for things they don't want scrutinised. The route bisects irreplaceable farmland. The poles and wires are larger than anything previously built in the region. And the consultation has been a tick-box exercise on a foregone conclusion.
argument.body: I am calling on the Government to stop this project immediately, table the underlying modelling, and put the underground alternative on the same level of disclosure as the overhead route before another acquisition notice is served on a Victorian farming family.
argument.quote: The people whose land is being taken should not be the last people consulted. We will not accept a process that treats Western Victoria as an empty corridor.
argument.planHeading: What I'm asking the Parliament to do
plan: Immediately halt all VNI West works, surveys and acquisition notices pending an independent route review.
Disclose, in full, every route-selection cost-benefit and environmental model relied on to date.
Cost the underground alternative on the same basis as the overhead route, and publish the comparison.
Establish a binding statutory community consultation right before any further land access.
Compensation parity with mining and pipeline easements, indexed for the life of the asset.
Independent assessment of the cumulative impact on farming communities across the entire corridor.
argument.whyBody: A petition tabled in the Legislative Council is filed publicly with my office and recorded in the Council's papers. Every name signed against this project is a name the Government has to walk past on its way into the chamber. The bigger the petition, the harder it becomes to keep ignoring.
